updates.title: Next.js 16.4.5, which fixes a known security vulnerability (GHSA-mfr8-8qww-v76h)
updates.whatToDo: The problem: Next.js 16.3.0 to 16.4.4 can give a visitor cached data that was made for another value of a root param, for example for another locale or another tenant (advisory GHSA-mfr8-8qww-v76h, CVE-2026-119790, severity moderate). It happens only when one function with `'use cache'` reads a root param and is called both directly and through `unstable_cache()`. The files of the boilerplate do not do that; the code of your project can. Next.js 16.4.3 also stops the first `next build` or `next dev` that an AI agent runs, with `SecurityFatalError`. The fix is Next.js 16.4.5. The command writes `16.4.5` for `next` and for `eslint-config-next` into the 6 `package.json` files and refreshes `package-lock.json`. Then do 3 things by hand: 1. Run `make install-js`. 2. In `apps/web/README.md` and `apps/internal/README.md`, change the row `| Next.js | 16.4.3 |` to `| Next.js | 16.4.5 |`, when your project kept that table. 3. Run `npm audit`, `make check` and `make e2e`: `npm audit` no longer names `next`. When your project chose another version of `next`, the command changes no file: write a version from 16.4.5 up by hand, the same one for `next` and `eslint-config-next`, and run `make install-js`.
